name: atr_expansion_breakout_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, institutional block orders (FII routing, VWAP algo completions, ETF rebalance flows) periodically create 5-second bars with range 2.5x+ the recent 10-minute ATR baseline. These are not random volatility spikes — they represent a genuine temporary imbalance between aggressive directional order flow and resting limit orders. When this expansion bar simultaneously creates a new session high (or low), the imbalance has overwhelmed ALL existing supply (or demand) accumulated since market open, signaling that the directional order flow is large enough to shift the session's price discovery level. NIFTY's high liquidity means the index can absorb most flows without such extreme bars — so when they occur, they carry information. The VWAP alignment and volume surge (2x+ the prior 5-minute average) confirm the expansion is institutional flow rather than a fat-finger or illiquidity artifact. Entry is on the expansion bar's close, betting that the flow that created the bar has not fully executed and will continue pushing the index for the next 30-90 seconds.

indicators.name: TR
indicators.formula: max(high - low, abs(high - prev_close), abs(low - prev_close))
indicators.purpose: True range captures the full bar's volatility including gaps. On NIFTY 5s bars, TR ≈ 2-8 spot points in normal conditions.

indicators.name: ATR_120
indicators.purpose: 120 bars = 10-minute rolling ATR baseline. NOT scaled from original's ATR(20) on 1-min (which would give 240 bars). Chosen because: (a) we target 30-90s holds, so the 'normal' volatility context should be the prior 10 minutes, not 20 minutes; (b) intraday NIFTY volatility clusters in 10-15 minute regimes (pre/post macro releases, FII routing windows); (c) 240 bars would lag too much when volatility regime shifts mid-session.

indicators.name: TR_ratio
indicators.purpose: Normalized expansion metric. Value > 2.5 means current bar's range is 2.5x the recent 10-min average — genuinely abnormal on NIFTY.

indicators.name: session_high
indicators.purpose: Cumulative session high — no lookback scaling needed. Breaking this level means the expansion bar overwhelmed ALL resistance accumulated since open.

indicators.name: session_low
indicators.purpose: Cumulative session low — symmetric to session_high.

indicators.name: VWAP
indicators.purpose: Cumulative session VWAP — no scaling needed. Used as directional filter: expansion bars above VWAP are bullish (institutional accumulation), below VWAP are bearish (institutional distribution).

indicators.name: volume_ratio
indicators.purpose: 60 bars = 5-min volume baseline. Scaled from original's SMA(20) on 1-min (= 20 min). Compressed to 5 min because at 5s resolution, a 20-min volume average would smooth out intraday volume surges and fail to detect genuine spikes. 5-min window reacts fast enough to flag unusual volume while stable enough to not flag every slightly-above-average bar.

conditions: TR_ratio > 2.5 (expansion bar: current TR is 2.5x the 10-min ATR baseline)
high > session_high[t-1] (new session high — overwhelms all prior supply)
close > open (bullish expansion bar: buyers controlled the bar)
(close - low) / (high - low) > 0.6 (closed in upper 40% of bar — strong bull close)
volume_ratio > 2.0 (volume at least 2x the prior 5-min average)
close > VWAP (in intraday bullish territory relative to VWAP benchmark)
buy_ce.confirmation: No follow-through bar required — unlike the original (1-min bars with 1-bar confirmation delay), at 5s resolution the expansion bar IS the signal. Waiting one more bar (5 seconds) would miss most of the continuation.

conditions: low < session_low[t-1] (new session low — overwhelms all prior support)
(high - close) / (high - low) > 0.6 (closed in lower 40% of bar — strong bear close)

entry.entry_price: limit order at expansion bar close

exit.stop_rationale: A 2.5x ATR expansion bar on NIFTY at 5s resolution typically has range 7-15 spot points (ATR_120 ≈ 3-6 spot pts, 2.5x = 7.5-15 pts). Entry is at the close (upper 40% of a bullish bar). Stop at midpoint = ~5-7 spot points below close = 2.5-3.5 option points at delta 0.5. We use 5 option points (slightly above midpoint equivalent) because if the expansion bar's midpoint breaks within 90 seconds, the institutional flow thesis has definitively failed. 5 pts gives just enough room for 2-3 bars of natural oscillation.
exit.target_rationale: Post-expansion continuation on NIFTY typically extends 1.0-1.5x the expansion bar's range in the next 30-90 seconds, as the underlying institutional order has not fully executed. At 10-15 spot pts expansion bar, continuation = 10-22 spot pts = 5-11 option pts. We target 8 pts = ~16 spot pts continuation, capturing the conservative end of the first continuation leg. This gives 1:1.6 R:R (5 stop : 8 target).

filters.vix_filter: none — VIX not used. ATR_120 already adapts to current volatility regime dynamically; high VIX sessions have higher ATR baselines so the 2.5x threshold self-adjusts.
filters.time_filter: 09:25-15:20 IST. Skip first 10 minutes (09:15-09:25): opening volatility creates many false ATR expansion bars as the market finds its level. Session end at 15:20 to avoid illiquid close dynamics.
filters.volume_filter: volume_ratio > 2.0 — mandatory confirmation that expansion is institutional flow, not illiquidity.
filters.trend_filter: VWAP alignment — ensures directional bias is consistent with intraday flow.
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at candle close prices, no spread cost.

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — as more algos recognize ATR expansion + session extreme as a signal, the patterns may front-run each other, reducing the continuation window. However, the underlying institutional flow is structural and cannot be arbed away.

adaptation_notes: Three key changes from original: (1) Dropped follow-through bar confirmation — at 5s resolution, the expansion bar close IS the signal; the 1-bar delay would sacrifice most of the 30-90s move. (2) ATR lookback compressed from ATR(20) on 1-min [20-min window] to ATR(120) on 5s [10-min window] — hold time is 6-18x shorter, so the volatility baseline should be proportionally more recent. (3) Volume baseline compressed from SMA(20) on 1-min [20-min window] to SMA(60) on 5s [5-min window] — same rationale, faster reaction needed. Session high/low and VWAP carry over unchanged as cumulative/session-level measures.
weaknesses: 2.5x ATR expansion bars are rare on NIFTY at 5s resolution (perhaps 2-6 per session meeting all conditions) — low trade frequency means higher variance of daily PnL
Entry on the expansion bar's close assumes the institutional order has NOT fully executed; if it has, the next bars see immediate mean reversion into the stop
Session high/low breakout condition means no signals during the first 10-20 minutes until a session high/low has been established that is meaningful
ATR_120 warmup requires 10 minutes of data at session start — no signals before 09:25
